results.title: Optimal convergence rates for the invariant density estimation of jump-diffusion processes | ESAIM: Probability and Statistics (ESAIM: P&S)
results.content: All issues Volume 26 (2022) ESAIM: PS, 26 (2022) 126-151 Abstract. ESAIM: PS 26 (2022) 126–151. ## Optimal convergence rates for the invariant density estimation of jump-diffusion processes. Chiara Amorino1\*,\*\* and Eulalia Nualart2,\*\*\*. \* Corresponding author: chiara.amorino@uni.lu. We aim at estimating the invariant density associated to a stochastic differential equation with jumps in low dimension, which is for *d* = 1 and *d* = 2. We consider a class of fully non-linear jump diffusion processes whose invariant density belongs to some Hölder space. Firstly, in dimension one, we show that the kernel density estimator achieves the convergence rate 1/*T*, which is the optimal rate in the absence of jumps. This improves the convergence rate obtained in Amorino and Gloter [*J. Inference* **213** (2021) 106–129], which depends on the Blumenthal-Getoor index for *d* = 1 and is equal to (log*T*)/*T* for *d* = 2. Secondly, when the jump and diffusion coefficients are constant and the jumps are finite, we show that is not possible to find an estimator with faster rates of estimation. Indeed, we get some lower bounds with the same rates {1/*T*, (log*T*)/*T*} in the mono and bi-dimensional cases, respectively. Finally, we obtain the asymptotic normality of the estimator in the one-dimensional case for the fully non-linear process. Key words: Minimax risk / convergence rate / non-parametric statistics / ergodic diffusion with jumps / Lévy driven SDE / invariant density estimation. results.title: Full article: Posterior rates of convergence for composite quantile regression
results.content: This article mainly aims to contribute to the theoretical justification of Bayesian composite quantile regression from the perspective of Bayesian density estimation. Zou and Yuan (Citation2008) showed that the relative efficiency of the CQR estimator relative to the LS estimator is at least 70% if we set for all *j*, since the strengths of multiple quantile regression models are combined. Huang and Chen (Citation2015) pointed out that the minimization problem (Equation2(2) (2) ) can be formulated as maximum likelihood estimation by assuming that the response *y**i* is a mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions (ALD), i.e., *y**i* has density. Sriram, Ramamoorthi, and Ghosh (Citation2013) proved posterior consistency of the Bayesian quantile regression estimator and derive the rate of convergence. Finite normal mixture is a popular model for density estimation, not only in the frequentist context but also in the Bayesian context. Ghosal and van der Vaart (Citation2001) derived the rate of convergence when the true density is a location or location-scale mixture of normal densities. Scricciolo (Citation2011) derived the rate of convergence for finite mixture and Dirichlet mixture of exponential power densities. The asymmetry parameter is now considered a vector with a unique element for each mixture component, misspecified, in a finite sample, relative to the assumed true density. In this article, we have studied asymptotic properties of mixtures of ALD with a specific interest in the composite quantile regression case, focusing on posterior convergence rates. We find that with the addition of an asymmetry parameter and the extension to part of the location being independent of the mixture, the convergence rates conform to those for the symmetric Laplace case as outlined in Scricciolo (Citation2011). Most importantly, the setting considered most realistic in terms of quantile regression in Theorem 2 had the same convergence rate as the mixture considered in Theorem 1. Such work should be closer in line with that of Sriram, Ramamoorthi, and Ghosh (Citation2013) on single quantile regression, for example, by restricting attention to a fixed, possibly small, number of mixture components. Bayesian density estimation by mixtures of normal distributions. Flexible Bayesian quantile curve fitting with shape restrictions under the Dirichlet process mixture of the generalized asymmetric Laplace distribution.
